title: Grateful Dead Live at Cincinnati Gardens on 1973-12-04
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording captures a short but stellar 12/4/73 show with crisp sound (aside from a minor balance issue) and a soaring 'Eyes of the World' jam.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD delivers generally clear, well‑balanced audio that lets the band's late‑night energy shine, though one reviewer notes a slight imbalance on "One More Saturday Night." Musically the concert is praised for its fiery early set, an unforgettable Truckin’ > Stella Blue transition and a dark, space‑y 23‑minute 'Eyes of the World' that showcases Garcia’s soaring leads and Lesh’s bass fireworks. Despite the tardy start and brief runtime, fans describe it as a quintessential fall ’73 performance.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are enthusiastic about the performance, highlighting multiple standout moments; recording is described as generally crisp with only minor balance quirks, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Overall clear and crisp soundboard capture; a few reviewers mention slight balance issues on 'One More Saturday Night' but no major drop‑outs or muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Late start leads to a short, high‑energy set that begins upbeat (Johnny B. Goode, Me & My Uncle) before diving into the dark, exploratory 'Eyes of the World' jam; finishes with concise rockers like Sugar Magnolia and One More Saturday Night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia delivers shredding leads on Johnny B. Goode, bright hopeful licks on Eyes of the World, and a space‑y duet with Phil during the extended jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh provides powerful bass 'bombs' that lock in with Garcia's improvisations, especially during the climax of Eyes of the World.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work and vocal harmonies are noted as part of the overall texture; no specific solo remarks.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux adds tasteful piano/organ colors, described as 'painting against the grain' in the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Kreutzmann is praised for his jack‑hammer snare work and driving the intensity during the Eyes of the World improvisation.
